Likely on your second or third PM role , with experience shipping real product and working closely with engineers. Strong product judgment, prioritization, and communication skills. Comfort operating in ambiguous environments where external systems are poorly documented, fragmented, or constantly changing. Genuine interest in AI product development, including how to evaluate model outputs, design human-in-the-loop workflows, and understand where LLMs break down. What You'll Need To Learn Quickly: How our platform automates benefit verification and prior authorization — the healthcare context that shapes every product decision. The external systems our product touches: EHRs, payer portals, PBM formularies, and NCPDP transaction standards. Our codebase, data model, and AI workflows — where quality is strong and where there's room to improve. Bonus Points: Experience working on AI-powered products or LLM-based workflows in production. Comfort with SQL, basic data analysis, or API concepts. Experience prototyping or shipping product changes directly with AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.). Experience in an early-stage startup where you had to move quickly and wear multiple hats. What We Offer: $160,000 – $200,000 base salary plus meaningful early-stage equity. Health, dental, and vision coverage, plus flexible PTO. High-end workstation and tooling budget. define the outcomes that matter; and make the tradeoffs needed to keep the roadmap focused. • Workshop with users and stakeholders — both to turn vague frustration into a clear problem statement, and to shape new features from the ground up. • Translate business needs into clear requirements, and stay accountable for them all the way through to a working feature — not just a written spec. • Build and own the backlog, and work directly with developers to turn requirements into shipped software. • Dig into raw data (JSON payloads, API responses, logs) across multiple systems yourself when you need an answer faster than waiting on someone else's ticket queue. • Identify and own dependencies across teams and systems — know what's blocking what, and drive it, rather than waiting for someone else to surface it. • Maintain a clear view across multiple concurrent workstreams, knowing where the important risks, decisions, dependencies, and blockers are - and be able to explain the real status without having to reconstruct it on the spot. • Build genuine working relationships with the people you depend on — because when you don't own the system, trust is what gets things unblocked. • Work effectively across time zones - engineering teams are primarily in Poland while client stakeholders are on the U.S. West Coast. You'll need to be deliberate about handoffs, written communication, and making the overlap hours count. • Act as a fallback layer of technical support on the product when something breaks and the usual path isn't fast enough. • Say no when something doesn't serve the roadmap, even when it's an easy yes to give. You’ll Thrive Here If You • Learn new domains fast and are comfortable operating in one before you've fully mastered it. • Can hold a strategic view and get into implementation details in the same conversation. • Are willing to form and share an opinion before you have complete information — and revise it in public when you're wrong. • Treat ambiguity as the normal condition of the job, not a blocker to raise up the chain. • Can bring calm and clarity to stakeholders even when the answer isn't obvious yet - and are comfortable saying what you know, what you don't know, and what you'll do next.
